thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Tech Rally Leads Stocks Higher As Inflation Concerns Wane

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Tech Rally Leads Stocks Higher As Inflation Concerns Wane
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Yield on 10-year note eases further, dollar sags
U.S. stocks rose on Monday, suggesting equities could extend a two-week rally as concerns appeared to fade about the inflation picture facing the economy and the impact it could have on interest rates.
Traders will be watching for comments from Fed officials in a week that will feature new Fed Chairman Jerome Powell's comments in front of Congress.
What are the main benchmarks doing
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 218 points, or 0.%, to 25,500. The S&P 500 rose 15 points to 2,762, a rise of 0.5%. The Nasdaq Composite Index climbed 45 points, or 0.6%, to 7,381. Both the Dow and S&P are on track for their third straight daily advance.
On Friday, all three gauges gained more than 1% (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-futures-climb-as-investors-wait-for-interest-rate-clues-from-fed-speakers-2018-02-23) as each benchmark notched its second positive week in a row. Friday represented the best day for the S&P in nearly three weeks.
What could drive markets?
Concerns that inflation could be returning to markets, and that the U.S. central bank may have to more aggressively raise interest rates to combat such a scenario, has been the primary driver of trading in recent weeks, even eclipsing a strong earnings season.
The fear recently pushed the Dow and S&P into correction territory, though they have recovered much of their lost ground, and now stand less than 5% below record levels. Last week, investors were heartened by a recent Federal Reserve report that gave little hint (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fed-on-track-for-3-rate-hikes-in-2018-but-4-no-sign-in-report-to-congress-2018-02-23) it was prepared to raise U.S. interest rates more aggressively this year, as has recently been a primary investor fear.
On Monday, St. Louis Fed President James Bullard said he doesn't think the so-called neutral U.S. interest rate is likely to rise much (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/feds-bullard-says-low-us-neutral-interest-rate-unlikely-to-rise-over-next-2-years-2018-02-26) over the next two years. Fed Vice Chairman Randall Quarles will speak on the same topic at the National Association of Business Economics in Washington at 3:15 p.m. Eastern.
But the main attraction this week will likely be Fed Chairman Jerome Powell, who will head to Capitol Hill on Tuesday for the first of two bouts of questions with U.S. lawmakers. Among other factors, investors want to know if the Fed is planning four interest-rate hikes for 2018 instead of three.
Read:Fed and new boss Jerome Powell are on inflation watch as anxious investors look on (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fed-and-new-boss-jerome-powell-are-on-inflation-watch-as-anxious-investors-look-on-2018-02-23)
Easing bond yields may also be giving stocks a lift. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note continue to pull lower on Monday, last at 2.84% from 2.871% late Friday.
Read:Why a spike in the 10-year Treasury yield to 3% won't be a death knell for stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/why-a-spike-in-the-10-year-treasury-yield-to-3-wont-be-a-death-knell-for-stocks-2018-02-24)
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/why-a-spike-in-the-10-year-treasury-yield-to-3-wont-be-a-death-knell-for-stocks-2018-02-24)In the latest economic data, the Chicago Fed national activity index came in at 0.12 in January, compared with 0.14 in the previous month.
A reading on new-home sales for January is due at 10 a.m. Eastern.
What are strategists saying?
"We're setting a stage for where we can live with a higher sense of inflation, but still have a market supported by fiscal policy. In other words, the consensus is that rates shouldn't go up at a rapid pace," said Frank Davis, director of sales and trading at LEK Securities. "There was a sense that the move down was overdue and perhaps a bit overdone, so it makes a little bit of sense that the move back up has been rapid as well."
Read:Stocks could plunge another 25% if this happens, warns Goldman Sachs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stocks-could-plunge-another-25-if-this-happens-warns-goldman-sachs-2018-02-26)
What stocks may be active?
The day's gains were broad, with 10 of the 11 primary S&P 500 sectors in solidly higher territory. The day's advance was driven by tech shares. Among the most notable gainers, Apple Inc.(AAPL) rose 1.2% while Intel Corp.(INTC) added 1.8%. Microsoft Corp.(MSFT) was up 0.8%.
"Tech has been a shining star, and to see a rotation into the sector seems healthy here," Davis said.
United Parcel Service Inc. (UPS) shares rose 0.7%. The package delivery service announced it is suing the European Union's antitrust watchdog for $2.15 billion plus interest (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ups-sues-eu-regulator-for-215-bln-over-tnt-deal-2018-02-26) over its decision to block a $7 billion merger with Dutch-based TNT Express NV in 2013.
Dean Foods Co.(DF) tumbled 16% after it reported fourth-quarter earnings (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dean-foods-shares-slide-10-premarket-after-earnings-miss-2018-02-26) that missed expectations and it also gave an outlook that was below forecasts.
AMC Networks Inc.(AMCX) agreed to buy RLJ Entertainment (RLJE) for $4.25 a share, a price that represents a premium of 9.8% to its Friday closing price. Shares of AMC were down 0.2% while RLJ jumped 8.5%.
Shares of Hibbett Sports Inc.(HIBB) sipped 0.8% despite the retailer raising its fourth-quarter guidance. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/hibbett-sports-shares-rise-after-guidance-increase-2018-02-26)
Gun makers could be volatile as more companies sever ties with the National Rifle Association. On Monday, Bank of America said it would would ask its clients (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/bank-of-america-asks-its-gunmaker-clients-how-they-can-end-mass-shootings-2018-02-26) who manufacture assault rifles how they can help end mass shootings, according to media reports. American Outdoor Brands Corp(AOBC) fell 2.4%.
How are other assets performing?
European stocks traded largely higher across the board (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-march-up-as-wall-street-looks-to-extend-rally-2018-02-26), while Asian equities closed in positive territory (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/nikkei-leads-asian-market-gains-as-yen-drops-2018-02-25).
The ICE U.S. Dollar Index was under pressure (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-skids-as-treasury-yields-head-lower-in-big-week-for-central-bankers-2018-02-26), down 0.3% to 89.647. Dollar weakness helped send gold higher (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-skids-as-treasury-yields-head-lower-in-big-week-for-central-bankers-2018-02-26), with the precious metal climbing $9.40, or 0.7%, to $1,339.70 an ounce. Crude-oil futures were down slightly, holding below $64 a barrel.
